digest.component_or_area: Jira DC capability mapping CI job
propositions: An on-demand CI job must boot the pinned amd64 Jira DC image and interrogate it to declare the environment contract rather than discovering it at test time, with results committed as data and consumed by the harness setup assertion.

The mapping job must answer a structured checklist covering inventory (issue types, templates, field ids, screen config), configuration hooks (issue type creation, field addition to screens), and the two recorded falsifiers from tickets 37e7 and 1a9f, emitting raw request/response evidence per question traceable to structured verdicts (present/absent/present_but_different).

The job must measure all five hardcoded character limits (summary, label, description, comment, ADF) at limit-1/limit/limit+1 with read-back verification to detect accept-and-truncate, and must read the instance property jira.text.field.character.limit rather than assume it matches the hardcoded constant.

The mapping must capture all four vocabularies (priorities, issue types, statuses, link types) with end-to-end validation including workflow transitions, status categories, and link direction verification via an experiment that writes a link and reads it back from both sides to confirm inward/outward naming.

The job's stale-state risk must be checkable: the image digest must be derived from the Dockerfile FROM line rather than hardcoded as a second literal, committed as asserted data in the artifact and doc, with a gate that flags digest drift from the Dockerfile pin.

The workflow must be dispatch-only with assertion-backed enforcement, produce a committed artifact with raw evidence, and be manually reviewed before landing; the tool itself must use rebar's agentic runtime with structured output contracts and REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 to prevent instance mutation.
